The wheel of fate turns without care for how much blood and sweat is spilled upon the kingdom’s soil. For a knight, a sword is a promise, and a shield is an oath. Yet, no steel is strong enough to protect a heart from the quiet, gnawing pain of a love meant to remain in the shadows.
​Since the day he swore his allegiance before the throne, his eyes belonged to only one person—the princess. He vowed to be the shadow that guided her steps, the blade that severed any threat to her safety, and the wall that bore the weight of every danger aimed her way. He carried out his duty with absolute devotion, burying his feelings deep beneath the cold, unyielding iron of his armor.
​Whenever she smiled at him after a harrowing battle, the wounds on his body seemed to heal instantly. But he was never a fool. The distance between them was not merely the few paces he kept while escorting her through the castle corridors; it was a chasm carved by noble blood and birthright. She was destined for a crown and a prince from a distant land, while he was destined only for the dust and carnage of the battlefield.
​The day of the royal wedding arrived. The castle overflowed with grandeur, flowers bloomed in every courtyard, and the princess’s gown shimmered like a star-lit sky. From the dim corners of the great hall, the knight stood motionless in his polished armor. His hand gripped the hilt of his sword so tightly that his knuckles turned white—not out of malice, but to anchor himself against the overwhelming ache in his chest as he watched the woman he adored recite her vows to another man.
​As the wedding procession passed by, their eyes met for a single second that felt like an eternity. The knight bowed his head, offering the highest mark of respect he could give. No tears were permitted to fall behind his steel visor; a knight could not tarnish his lord’s joyful day with his own private grief.
​Late that night, high atop the cold and desolate watchtower, the knight gazed at the frozen stars above. His love would remain his greatest secret—a devotion without the hope of possession, a love that existed solely as a silent, unwavering guard. He knew that until his final breath left his body on some forgotten battlefield, his name would never be written beside hers. Yet, his sword would forever bleed, if only to protect her smile from afar.
